questions.question: Use GRANT options to construct a privilege-propagation scenario involving users A1,A2 and A3? / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Use GRANT options to construct a privilege-propagation scenario involving users A1,A2
  • and A3 : - The GRANT statement is used to provide privileges to users. The WITH GRANT
  • OPTION allows a user to pass the granted privileges to other users. .
  • Eg . Scenario
  • Assume user A1 owns a table named STUDENT and wants to grant privileges to A2 and A3.
  • Step 1: A1 grants privileges to A2
  • GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON STUDENT TO A2 WITH GRANT OPTION;
  • A1 grants SELECT and INSERT privileges to A2. Since WITH GRANT OPTION is specified,
  • A2 can grant these privileges to other users.
  • Step 2: A2 grants SELECT privilege to A3
  • GRANT SELECT ON STUDENT TO A3;
  • A2 grants the SELECT privilege to A3. A3 can retrieve records from the STUDENT table
  • but cannot grant the privilege to another user because WITH GRANT OPTION was not specified.

questions.question: Implement a checkpoint in a given transaction log and illustrate how it reduces recovery work. / [CO3] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Implement a checkpoint in a given transaction log and illustrate how it reduces recovery
  • work.
  • A checkpoint is a recovery mechanism in DBMS that records a known point in the transaction
  • log so that the system can reduce the amount of log information it needs to examine after a
  • system crash.
  • Without checkpoints, the recovery manager may need to scan a large portion of the log from the
  • beginning. With checkpoints, it can usually start from a more recent recovery point, while still
  • examining any earlier records required by the recovery protocol.
  • Write example of Transaction Log and write implementation of Checkpoint record into
  • transaction log . And also write how it reduces recovery work.
